business_problem: Scam proceeds can be moved through money-mule accounts before victims report fraud, making the funds difficult to trace. Banks also need reliable evidence to identify suspect accounts and intervene without generating a flood of false alerts.
solution_summary: Cybera's Money Mule Intelligence uses AI-generated personas that pose as believable potential victims, engage scammers, and continue conversations until a payment request reveals the receiving account details. Cybera says it operates hundreds of personas across thousands of conversations every day, identifying accounts while they are still active rather than after a victim reports a loss. Cybera verifies each account and attaches evidence and context to the intelligence, giving bank fraud teams more than a risk score when they decide whether to intervene. The service is available through Recorded Future, which gives financial institutions access to the account intelligence. In the described European private-bank example, the receiving account was checked against confirmed scam accounts in real time and the bank stopped a €60,000 transfer. The page does not identify conversation platforms, AI models, data interfaces, or storage architecture; it describes no separate ingestion or persistence products.
